Both [[credential-scoping]] and [[runtime-paths]] implement the same architectural
principle: centralized, single-phase setup at Hub startup that prevents distributed
decision-making downstream.

**Credential Scoping** ensures that the Anthropic API key never enters the Hub's own
process environment. Instead, a secrets loader reads the key exactly once at startup
and injects it into each spawned child process's environment immediately before that
child starts — never earlier, never more broadly.

**Runtime Path Resolution** ensures that every file-system location the Hub will touch
is discovered, validated, and resolved in exactly one place at startup. No part of the
codebase is allowed to re-discover paths or read the ambient working directory later;
downstream code consumes the already-resolved path set.

The connection: both decisions defer their core logic to the same critical moment — the
Hub's initialization phase — so that:

1. **Security-critical decisions are centralized.** The Hub's startup phase is the right
   place to enforce credential boundaries and path validation before any agent (or any
   potentially untrusted code path) runs. This prevents a sprawl of independent
   credential-injection or path-resolution logic scattered across the codebase, each of
   which would be another surface for attack or misconfiguration.

2. **The composition point becomes a gating function.** Once startup completes, the
   process environment and resolved paths form a read-only, already-validated snapshot.
   Downstream code cannot request new credentials or discover new paths; it can only
   use what was provisioned at composition time. This is a form of capability scoping
   that mirrors the principle of least privilege.

3. **Adding a new runtime resource requires extending one resolver, not scattering
   logic.** Whether the new resource is a path, a credential, or another form of
   configuration, the architectural pattern is the same: declare the requirement in
   the central resolver, validate it at startup, and provide it as an immutable value
   downstream. This scales the security model as the system grows.

In essence, credential-scoping and runtime-paths are two instances of the same pattern:
**single-phase, centralized composition** as a security boundary and a scalability lever.
